precepts.text: These things hast thou done, and I kept silence; thou thoughtest that I was altogether such an one as thyself: but I will reprove thee, and set them in order before thine eyes. As a result of all this enslavement and all these massacres, Esau is thinking a certain way now. He thinks he is getting away with it. Oh, wait a minute, we just enslaved the Lord's people and he did not do anything. Thou thoughtest that I was altogether such an one as thyself. That is what Esau is thinking to this day. This is why they do not hold themselves accountable for anything. They hold themselves not guilty when they slay us, when they kill us, when they put us into slavery, when they do not give us reparations. Esau thinks he is God. But I will reprove thee: there will be a judgment for these things.
precepts.point: They were a naughty generation. They are naughty people. And that their malice was bred in them. You know what that means? God made them that way. He put that in them. And that their cogitation would never be changed. They will never change as a race of people. That is why it has been a perpetual hatred from Cain to Abel, Jacob to Esau, blacks and whites. It just keeps playing itself out over and over again. But Christianity blinds us from it, so that we will not accept what God is telling us there. It is in them. The malice is bred in them and their thought process will never change.
precepts.why:
Why is it that when our iniquity had an end, Esau refused to let us go and kept shedding our blood? Solomon speaks of the ancient Egyptians, and this is modern Egypt today: “not being ignorant that they were a naughty generation, and that their malice was bred in them, and that their cogitation would never be changed.” Their malice is bred in them: God made them that way. They will never change as a race of people. That's why it has been a perpetual hatred from Cain to Abel, Jacob to Esau, blacks and whites, playing itself out over and over, while Christianity blinds us from accepting what God is telling us.

Name a century that black people have had pure peace around this white man. Not we-got-the-vote peace: you still get jailed, racially profiled, shot down, and you can't do what white people do when they get pulled over. The record lists it: the transatlantic slave trade and child slavery from 1619 to 1865, racial terror after emancipation, massacres in Memphis, Colfax, Wilmington, Atlanta, East St. Louis, the Red Summer, Arkansas, Tulsa, Rosewood. And that is only what was reported; imagine what was not documented.

As a result of all this enslavement and all these massacres, Esau is thinking a certain way now. He thinks he's getting away with it: “These things hast thou done, and I kept silence.” Oh, wait a minute, we just enslaved the Lord's people and he didn't do anything.

“thou thoughtest that I was altogether such an one as thyself.” That is what Esau is thinking to this day. That's why they don't hold themselves accountable for anything. They hold themselves not guilty when they slay us, when they kill us, when they put us into slavery, when they don't give us reparations. Esau thinks he is God.

“but I will reprove thee, and set them in order before thine eyes.” There will be a judgment for these things. So don't think that smiling white man in your face means to do you good.

precepts.text: Thou hast had a perpetual hatred and hast shed the blood of the children of Israel in the time of their calamity; while we struggle they are still killing us, a woman who called the police for help murdered in her own house.
precepts.point: It was a cursed seed from the beginning, and no pardon for any of those things: there is no grace for Esau, his neck stays on the chopping block, and nothing he does can change it.
precepts.why:
Wisdom says the Lord gave the ungodly “place of repentance, not being ignorant that they were a naughty generation, and that their malice was bred in them”. Their malice is their hatred for us, shown in all the sins they have committed against us, and it is still going on: innocent blood shed again in Springfield, Illinois, a woman who called the police for help and ended up murdered in her own house. How do you call the police for help and they kill you?

Ezekiel names that malice: “Because thou hast had a perpetual hatred, and hast shed the blood of the children of Israel by the force of the sword in the time of their calamity, in the time that their iniquity had an end”. While we are here struggling and suffering, they are still killing us.

That is why the Lord executes judgment on them “by little and little”: a flood here, a fire there, an earthquake here, a war there. He is not ignorant of what they are; he created them, so he knows their pedigree. “Their cogitation would never be changed”: their way of thinking, the hatred they have for us, cannot change. That is why the cop shot the man and said he did not even know why he shot him. It is in them.

It was there from the beginning: “And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing wherewith his father blessed him: and Esau said in his heart, The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then will I slay my brother Jacob.” He made up his mind from young to kill Jacob, and that thought has continued from generation to generation. It started with Cain and Abel, for Esau is Cain regenerated. That is the perpetual hatred.

“For it was a cursed seed from the beginning; neither didst thou for fear of any man give them pardon”. There is no pardon and no grace for Esau. His neck is on the chopping block, and the judgment coming to America will not change however much they jump, yell and shout. This land is Esau’s kingdom and we are just living in it, so do not set your affection on it.

precepts.text: Executing thy judgments upon them by little and little: a war here, a storm here, a plague there. Not being ignorant that they were a naughty generation, and that their malice was bred in them, and that their cogitation would never be changed: their hatred was baked in from the creation, and their way of thinking will never change. For it was a cursed seed from the beginning: Cain was cursed from the beginning, and Esau was cursed from the beginning. Neither didst thou for fear of any man give them pardon for those things wherein they sinned: no matter what they do, they can never be pardoned for the sins they have committed. Even the killings where the officer himself cannot say why he shot a man lying flat with his hands up: sometimes they do things they do not even know why they do.
precepts.point: Behold, his soul which is lifted up is not upright in him: something is wrong with that man; the Most High created him that way.
precepts.why:
Habakkuk says, “Behold, his soul which is lifted up is not upright in him”. Something is wrong with that man; he is not normal. Wisdom of Solomon shows Esau: “But executing thy judgments upon them by little and little, thou gavest them place of repentance”. By little and little: a war here, a war there, a storm here, a tsunami there, a plague here, a plague there.

“Not being ignorant that they were a naughty generation, and that their malice was bred in them, and that their cogitation would never be changed.” A naughty generation, like the border of wickedness. Their hatred was bred in them: when God created them, a couple of drops of hatred, put in the oven and baked, and you cannot get it out of the dough. Their cogitation, their way of thinking, their mind frame, will never change. The Lord created him that way.

Sometimes they do things they don't even know why they do. In Florida a man caring for handicapped kids lay flat on the ground with his hands up, and the cop shot him; asked why, the cop said, I don't know. In the South bodies are found hanging and the judgment is suicide, as if our brothers had superpowers to tie their own hands behind their backs and dunk their necks into the noose.

“For it was a cursed seed from the beginning”. Not a blessed seed: Cain was cursed from the beginning, and he came back as Esau, cursed from the beginning. “Neither didst thou for fear of any man give them pardon for those things wherein they sinned.” They cannot be pardoned. Their malice is bred in them, they are cursed from the beginning, their cogitation will never change, and no matter what they do they can never be pardoned for the sins they have committed. Your pastor done lied to you.

precepts.text: The old inhabitants of the holy land were hated for odious works of witchcraft, wicked sacrifices, merciless murders of children, devouring of man's flesh and feasts of blood, and Manasseh did worse than they.
precepts.point: Manasseh made Judah err and do worse than the heathen the Lord had destroyed before them, the nations Joshua and the elders were sent to kill out of the land for the very same works.

note.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

precepts.why:
“So Manasseh made Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem to err, and to do worse than the heathen, whom the Lord had destroyed before the children of Israel.” Worse than the nations we were killing out of the land for doing the exact same thing. What does that mean? Wisdom of Solomon gives an idea.

“For it was thy will to destroy by the hands of our fathers both those old inhabitants of thy holy land”. Our fathers were Joshua, Caleb and the elders who succeeded Moses; when we entered the promised land we had to war with the nations already there. The old inhabitants were the Canaanites, the Hamites living in the land before we got there.

“Whom thou hatedst for doing most odious works of witchcrafts, and wicked sacrifices”: odious works are filth, evil, vile things, and that is what Manasseh was doing. “And also those merciless murderers of children”: Manasseh did it and had the people do it. “and devourers of man’s flesh, and the feasts of blood”: cannibalism, drinking blood, eating flesh. Who knows what Manasseh was doing, but he was worse than the heathen, so we have to factor this in. “and the parents, that killed with their own hands souls destitute of help”: we were killing our own kids.

“That the land, which thou esteemedst above all other, might receive a worthy colony of God’s children.” The Lord had us go in and kill those nations out of the land because they were doing these things. Then we got the land, turned around, and did the exact same thing and worse under Manasseh, as Ahab did in his time. Manasseh was one of the worst kings Judah ever had.
